newsitem.title: KENYA: Sudan rebel leader eyes Juba, rejects talks.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebel leader eyes Juba, rejects talks.

text.p: Sudanese rebel leader John Garang said on Monday his forces had escalated a military campaign to topple the Islamist government in Khartoum and were now circling Juba, the capital of the war-torn south.

Garang, head of the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), told a news conference in the Kenyan capital Nairobi that opposition groups in Africa's largest country had also managed to consolidate political and diplomatic pressure against Khartoum.
"We are moving around Juba and encircling it...and the city is within artillery range," Garang said.
Asked why his forces had not seized Juba, Garang said it was because of humanitarian considerations.
Garang's forces and northern allies in the opposition National Democratic Alliance (NDA) have launched a series of successful offensives this year and recaptured a string of towns and villages.
The NDA launched attacks into Sudan from Eritrea in January, initially capturing several towns and prompting Sudan to order a general mobilisation which halted the rebel advance.
"We want to be sure that when we attack Juba it is with a precision on military targets," added the veteran guerrilla leader.

Garang was speaking ahead of the Inter-Governmental Authority on Development (IGAD) regional summit to take place in Kenya on July 8 and 9. It will tackle the civil war in Sudan and the country's stormy ties with neighbouring Eritrea, Ethiopia and Uganda.
IGAD groups those five countries, as well as Somalia and Djibouti, and aims to help settle conflicts in the region.
Garang dismissed Sudanese media reports that he would hold direct talks with military leader Lieutenant-General Omar Hassan Al-Bashir on the sidelines of the IGAD summit.
The Sudan government newspaper Al-Anbaa reported on Friday that American, European and African efforts were underway to arrange a meeting between Garang and Al-Bashir at the IGAD summit.

"Holding talks with Al-Bashir...will not happen. Such a meeting can only serve to strengthen Bashir's propaganda machine. I know he wants a handshake for his propaganda but he will not have it," Garang said.
In April, Sudan signed an accord with a number of factions intended to end civil war.
The SPLA has fought since 1983 for greater autonomy of the Christian and animist south from the Moslem, Arabised north.

In the Eritrean capital Asmara, an official of the SPLA said a senior Sudanese government official along with several administrators, had fled the town of Damazine and joined rebels in the southern Blue Nile area.
SPLA spokesman, Yassir Arman, said the executive director of the Blue Nile state and six of his officers had joined SPLA forces.
